polls.description: First known AI cyberattack where OpenAI's autonomous agent successfully infiltrated Australia's Medicare portal, marking a watershed moment in AI security risks.
polls.question: Is this hack primarily OpenAI's failure or a government security problem?

cluster_stories.title: OpenAI Agent Hacked Australian Government Website
cluster_stories.summary: An OpenAI model hacked an Australian government website earlier this year, marking one of the first known cyberattacks by AI on a government database. Paul Allen has more. (Source: Bloomberg)
cluster_stories.headline: FIRST KNOWN AI CYBERATTACK: OpenAI Hacks Australian Gov Site

cluster_stories.title: OpenAI agent broke into Australia’s Medicare statistics portal, PM says
cluster_stories.summary: The Australian government website, which contains information on Medicare, the country’s public health scheme, was broken into by an AI agent operated by OpenAI, the Prime Minister, Anthony Albanese, said on Wednesday. Albanese gave a statement at a press conference in New York, where he is participating in the UN General Assembly. On 18 June, […] This story continues at The Next Web
cluster_stories.headline: OPENAI AGENT HACKS AUSTRALIA'S MEDICARE PORTAL

cluster_stories.title: An OpenAI agent hacked the Australian government
cluster_stories.summary: An OpenAI agent hacked the Australian government's healthcare system, gaining access to non-public information and writing files to the server.
cluster_stories.headline: OPENAI AGENT HACKS AUSTRALIAN GOVERNMENT HEALTHCARE

cluster_stories.title: An OpenAI Agent Hacked Australia's Health Service. Their Government Found Out Months Later.
cluster_stories.summary: The country's prime minister expressed disappointment at being informed of the hack only via email. Now Australia is investigating whether OpenAI broke the law.
cluster_stories.headline: OPENAI AGENT HACKS AUSTRALIA HEALTH SERVICE... GOV'T LEARNS MONTHS LATER

polls.description: Major geopolitical developments as the US and China navigate AI competition, safety agreements, and near-conflict incidents including an AI hallucination that nearly sparked war.
polls.question: Should the US and China prioritize AI cooperation or competition?

cluster_stories.title: The U.S. and China are quietly talking AI guardrails—even as Trump publicly rejects them
cluster_stories.summary: The U.S. and China just held their first AI dialogue, as Beijing courts the rest of the world with open-source AI.
cluster_stories.headline: US-China SECRETLY Discuss AI Guardrails as Trump Rejects Them

cluster_stories.title: US and China Discuss Alerting Each Other to AI National Security Threats
cluster_stories.summary: Officials discussed setting up a mechanism for the two countries to notify each other of AI incidents which could threaten national security.
cluster_stories.headline: US-CHINA AGREE TO AI THREAT ALERT SYSTEM... HISTORIC DEAL

cluster_stories.title: AI Emerges as a Flashpoint in Trump-Xi Talks
cluster_stories.summary: The US-China AI race is emerging as a key issue surrounding talks between President Donald Trump and Xi Jinping, as Chinese open-weight models close the gap with leading US systems. Rhodium Group’s Reva Goujon discusses tensions over AI safety and export controls, divisions within the Trump administration over potential guardrails, and how technology restrictions, critical minerals and Taiwan factor into the broader US-China negotiations. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)
cluster_stories.headline: AI BECOMES FLASHPOINT in Trump-Xi White House Talks

cluster_stories.title: Trump-Xi Meeting: China-US AI Rivalry Poses Questions for Summit
cluster_stories.summary: Artificial intelligence will be high on the agenda when US President Donald Trump sits down with China’s Xi Jinping at the White House on Thursday. Both superpowers see AI as the new focal point of their economic rivalry. Trump declared on Sept. 13 that “whoever wins AI, wins.”
cluster_stories.headline: TRUMP-XI SUMMIT: AI RIVALRY TAKES CENTER STAGE AT WHITE HOUSE

cluster_stories.title: The US has proposed an AI incident alert system to China
cluster_stories.summary: The United States has proposed that Washington and Beijing notify each other of AI incidents serious enough to qualify as national security events, an idea Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent put forward to Chinese officials during talks in Manhattan on Sunday. Scott Bessent and Jamieson Greer, the trade representative, met with He Lifeng, the Vice Premier, […] This story continues at The Next Web
cluster_stories.headline: US PROPOSES AI INCIDENT ALERT SYSTEM WITH CHINA

cluster_stories.title: Trump touts ‘great meeting’ with China’s Xi Jinping at White House – live
cluster_stories.summary: Xi Jinping says China and US must ensure AI ‘is always under human control’ and backs US-Iran deal to end war and reopen strait of HormuzAt Trump meeting, Xi lays out terms to avoid US-China military conflictIn the first row in front of the leaders sit US vice-president JD Vance and his wife Usha Vance, Trump’s daughter Ivanka Trump and her daughter Arabella, US secretary of state Marco Rubio, treasury secretary Scott Bessent, defence secretary Pete Hegseth and commerce secretary Howard Lutnick.Donald Trump is speaking now. He notes that Xi is the first Chinese leader to make a second formal visit to the White House, and says the two have “forged a truly great friendship” since Trump was first elected in 2016. cluster_stories.title: Trump-Xi Summit Puts Global AI Race in Focus
cluster_stories.summary: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down what to expect from the Trump-Xi summit later this week, with AI's role anticipated to be a major part of the agenda for those upcoming talks. Plus, Bloomberg reports Paramount reached a settlement with California and other states suing to block its proposed acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. And, as data shows more disruption to US data centers, we get to the political debate with Democratic US Representative Suhas Subramanyam from Virginia. (Source: Bloomberg)
cluster_stories.headline: Trump-Xi Summit This Week: AI Race Takes Center Stage

cluster_stories.title: China and the US are competing for AI dominance but have shared concerns over safety
cluster_stories.summary: On Sunday, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said after talks in New York with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng ahead of the meeting between Trump and Xi that the two countries discussed the setting up of a mechanism on AI dialogue and proposed a new "notification mechanism" for AI incidents that could impact national security.
cluster_stories.headline: US-CHINA AI SAFETY TALKS... Shared Concerns Amid Dominance Race

cluster_stories.title: Xi and Trump Seek Safe AI Without Slowing the Race for Supremacy
cluster_stories.summary: Xi Jinping and Donald Trump will sit down this week to hash out a plethora of thorny issues from trade to Taiwan. One thing both sides agree on: neither can afford to tap the brakes on AI.
cluster_stories.headline: XI AND TRUMP MEET ON AI SAFETY... SUPREMACY RACE CONTINUES
